mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (measured as month-over-month change) signals an easing monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines (month-over-month), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that increase corporate earnings uncertainty, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal a contraction in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% and remaining elevated for 3 months), the Federal Reserve's policy stance reduces liquidity and increases borrowing costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past month signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS growth and 20-day SPX returns is not significantly positive (Rank IC < 0.05) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) fall below 370,000 million dollars in a month, it indicates weakening consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when RSAFS < 370000.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decreases in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signal a strong labor market that boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline does not produce positive returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market downturn (defined by HOUST falling below 950,000 units for two consecutive months), weak housing activity reduces consumer wealth and construction investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 950000 for two consecutive months.
